perspective:
**Alice Lim — available information from her perspective**

- She knows Austin Moreno as an old friend from high school; they have a close friendship, discuss their personal/professional lives, and support each other.
- She knows her own healthcare/dental-hygiene background and experience.
- She observed Austin becoming reserved when work came up. This made her concerned and curious, and she suspected he might be hiding something about his job performance. She invited him to coffee.
- At coffee, she asked if everything was okay at the office. She heard Austin say it was nothing really, just usual ups and downs; later he said he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and that it was complicated. She told him he could talk to her.
- After that conversation, she believed Austin might be considering a career change because of dissatisfaction at work. She felt worried about his well-being and decided to share her own experiences and discuss healthcare career paths.
- She asked Austin if he had thought about changing careers. She heard him say he had thought about it but didn’t know what other paths he could take, and he asked for her suggestion. She told him healthcare needs dedicated people, offered to tell him more, and offered contacts. She heard him say it sounded interesting and that he wanted to know more about her experiences and what it involves.
- She sensed Austin was hesitant about changing careers because of fear of the unknown; she felt frustration and empathy. She told him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. She heard Austin say that was inspiring but that he worried about risks and the initial struggle. She told him those feelings were natural, growth comes from stepping out of comfort zones, and she would support him. She heard him thank her and say it helped knowing he had her support and hearing real success stories.
- Seeing his openness, she felt encouraged and hopeful. She suggested he talk to a career counselor and offered to connect him with friends in healthcare. She heard him say that would be helpful and that he appreciated the connections. She said it was about taking first steps and that she would set up a meeting next week. She heard him thank her and say he was looking forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, she believed Austin was ready to take the next steps and appreciated her help. She felt satisfaction and joy. She told him she was proud of his steps and asked how he felt. She heard him say he felt excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. She suggested regular check-ins. She heard him agree, saying it would keep him focused and that her perspective was good. She plans regular check-ins with him.
- She does not have direct access to Austin’s unspoken private thoughts or motives; she only knows what he said and what she inferred from his behavior.
